name: Epithelial Recurrent Erosion Dystrophy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Epithelial Recurrent Erosion Dystrophy

criteria.description: Recurrent episodes of corneal epithelial erosions confirmed by slit-lamp examination
Presence of subepithelial corneal scarring or microcysts on slit-lamp biomicroscopy
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Corneal topography showing irregular epithelial surface and localized thinning

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of recurrent corneal epithelial erosions and characteristic subepithelial corneal changes on slit-lamp examination
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not routinely required

imaging: Slit-lamp biomicroscopy showing recurrent epithelial erosions and subepithelial microcysts
Corneal topography demonstrating epithelial irregularities and localized thinning
other: Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance pattern

distinguishingFeatures: Characteristic map, dot, and fingerprint patterns on corneal epithelium
Less frequent recurrent erosions compared to epithelial recurrent erosion dystrophy
Amyloid deposits in corneal stroma visible on slit-lamp
Progressive stromal opacities rather than primarily epithelial erosions

redFlags: Sudden onset of severe ocular pain with vision loss
Signs of secondary infection such as purulent discharge
references: Krachmer JH, Mannis MJ, Holland EJ. Cornea. 4th ed. Elsevier; 2011.
Orphanet: Epithelial recurrent erosion dystrophy - ORPHA:293381
American Academy of Ophthalmology Preferred Practice Pattern: Recurrent Corneal Erosions, 2019
